title: The KKK Club and his many day jobs in Ottumwa
summary: The band had the Klub Klee Klo gig and every other job in town; Gus worked in a furniture store, as a busboy and barber while sending money home.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Oh, sure, sure. I enjoyed that, you know. And we had a lot of fun. And we had all the jobs sewed up in this town, like, we worked at the club. The club was called KKK. Klub Klee Klo. But we called it the KKK Club, see.
Right.
And, like, Leonard Chadwick, he was working at Harte's Furniture Store. I was working at Harte's Furniture Store during the day.
Oh, you were rolling in money, Gus.
Plus I was busboy at a hotel, --
No kidding.
-- the only hotel they had there.
You had energy to spare in those days.
And John, he was working at a filling station, except Little Johnny, he was -- he didn't work any-place because he was going to school. He was the baby, see.
Yeah, yeah.
And Spec, he only played at the club.
Yeah.
And the bass player, he had him a extra job, too. He worked at a garage. And if anybody wanted a job, they had to come see us before they could get a job.
You had it all sewed up.
Had it all sewed up. And I was cutting hair on top of that.
Gus, isn't that funny?
I had as many customers as the regular barber, coming to see me.
Well, where did you learn?
I learned just --
Just as you went along.
Just as I went along, by working in barbershops, you know, one of these things.
Fancy that.
See, I used to shine shoes and all like that. All that came up as I came up in Houston, and Dallas and all like that.
And as I say, we didn't really talk about it, but those were Depression days, so that anybody was glad of any work they could get.
That's right, see.
You learned to do anything you could do.
And I didn't mind doing it.
No, that was good.
I enjoyed it.
Well, but I'll tell you, you must have been pretty strong to do all that. I mean, what sort of hours did the band keep?
Well, we worked from -- say, like, 9:00 at night until 2:00 in the morning.
And of course, in a way, you enjoyed it so much.
Oh, sure.
It isn't exactly like hard work.
It wasn't all that hard.
Because you were doing what you wanted to do, anyway.
Sure. I even worked for the Three
Sisters. You know the Three Sisters clothing store, when they first started?
No kidding?
Worked for them in Ottumwa.
Fancy that. Well, now, you weren't married by then, were you?
Oh, no.
No.
No, I wasn't married then.
Yeah.
I was single.
You had a lot of gold coming in, one way or another.
